## The class multiverse

```{r}
#| label: spec-curve
#| fig-width: 9.5
#| fig-height: 4.3
# The curve of the claim, the chart that the Specification curve page draws, minus the
# hover: the specifications ranked by the claim-aligned partial r and classed
# by CR2 errors clustered by country, with the reproduced specification
# (the model of C6HJR) tagged in ink. Built on spec_base() (setup chunk), so that the
# next slide reuses this exact panel.
spec_base() +
  mark_layer(dplyr::transmute(curve_ref, rank, r = r_ca, sig,
                              label = paste0("reproduced specification\nCR2 p = ", fmt_num(p_cr2, 4))))
```

::: {.small}
- The curve of the claim: **`r format(nrow(spec_curve), big.mark = ",")`** specifications of the three positive scales – unemployment or GDP growth, two fixed-effects designs, and the measurement options that the review keeps
- **`r fmt_pct(share_below(spec_curve))`** below zero, **`r fmt_pct(share_sig(spec_curve))`** below zero with CR2 p < 0.05, and the claim-aligned partial r runs from **`r fmt_num(min(spec_curve$r_ca))` to +`r fmt_num(max(spec_curve$r_ca))`**
:::

::: {.src}
data/spec_curve.csv: the height of a mark is the partial r of the conventional fit, its shape the class under CR2 errors clustered by country, on Satterthwaite df.
:::

::: notes
This is the curve of the claim, over which the Class results page has been drawing your dots. The eight hundred and sixty-four specifications are ranked from the strongest support for the claim on the left to the weakest on the right, and every one is a justifiable answer to the claim. Almost all of them lie below zero, the direction of the claim, so the disagreement does not concern the direction. The shape of a mark shows the test, a circle where errors clustered by country, with the CR2 correction, give a p under point zero five and a cross where they do not, and about three in four are circles. The reproduced specification, my own model, is a cross, with a CR2 p of point zero five zero four. Where did the class results fall, did anyone end above zero, and which choice moved your estimate most? [pause for answers]
:::

## The published results on the curve {#where-your-result-lands}

```{r}
#| label: spec-overlay
#| fig-width: 9.5
#| fig-height: 4.3
# The same panel as the previous slide, with the six reference results
# (data/reference_marks.csv) placed as the chart at the top of the Multiverse
# page places them: each on the degrees of freedom of its own inference, in
# ink, its shape from the CR2 check where the design can be refitted on
# the country-year cells and from the p-value as reported where it cannot.
# The C6HJR mark is the reproduced specification itself.
spec_base() +
  mark_layer(dplyr::transmute(ref_marks, rank, r = r_placement, sig, label = tag))
```

::: {.resultline}
Your own dots are on the class chart of the [Class results]({{< var live-results-url >}}) page, drawn over this same curve
:::

::: {.src}
data/reference_marks.csv: each result on the degrees of freedom of its own inference, OA and PRL47 on the Satterthwaite df of the workshop's refit of each design.
:::

::: notes
The same chart carries the six reference results, the five analysts of the robustness study and the design of the original author, tagged OA design, each placed on the degrees of freedom of its own inference, as the background page explains. KEVF1, KQXUE and the original design sit to the left, with between a sixth and a third of the curve further below zero, and my own result is the reproduced specification. PRL47 sits further right once its z is converted on the degrees of freedom of the workshop's refit of its design, and 018OL lies near the right-hand end. Four of the six come from outside the menu, so they are drawn from a wider space than this curve, and none of them is wrong. Your own dots are on the Class results page over the same curve, so keep it open beside this one and find yourself.
:::
